text: Both requirements are scoped. Now the first real architecture decision: what actually gets built, and in which tool.

Kafka decouples the scanners and GPS trackers from everything downstream. Databricks and Delta Lake own the governed historical lakehouse. Fabric provides two separate surfaces, not one, because trend analytics and live status are genuinely different jobs.
A single bigger warehouse would fix Operations' freshness problem and do nothing for Support's two-minute requirement -- it was never built for live point lookups.
Nothing about this requires replacing a single scanner or GPS tracker, and the existing CSV export keeps running until the new tables are proven.
Next: designing the actual Kafka event schema -- what a scan or GPS event contains, field by field.
